A lot of stories I see about reddit (and Voat), many of them linked on this subverse, refer to the reddit administrator's desire for the site to "mature."

Restricting speech, telling people what is or is not okay to post after being an open platform for years, throwing hissy fits with new rules and banning subs or shadowbanning users... those are not the actions of a mature company. Maturity is being able to tolerate - not accept, but tolerate - views that may be disagreeable or offensive. Maturity is being able to say, "I think what you said is reprehensible, but you have the right to believe whatever you like." I think the Confederate flag is a symbol of rich white slaveowners who thought they were above the rule of law (and got their asses handed to them by the Union hoo-rah), but if someone believes differently, I don't take it personally... because I'm a god-damn adult human being with a functioning brain (sorry if I'm being ableist). FPH and coontown and SRS - full of hateful idiots I want nothing to do with, but I'm fine with them having a voice on Reddit, because that's what Reddit was supposed to be. Can you doxx somone on reddit? No, and you can't yell "Fire!" in a crowded theater, either. There are limits, which are necessary, but reddit is going too far and infantilizing the site by removing anything remotely offensive or challenging, and takes away the opportunity to engage with people who think differently, which is increasingly important as our culture segregates itself further and further into its tribes.

Being a grown-ass adult in this country means you don't have the right to not be offended, but you do have the right to argue, counter, and fight back against speech with which you disagree. The only proper response to someone saying something offensive is to counter it with alternative ideas. I switched to Voat because reddit doesn't believe that anymore and this site does. Varying opinions are important, even if they're unpopular. Reddit, of course, has every right to say "We don't want these opinions on our site." But after holding themselves up as a free speech forum for so long, to suddenly change gears and declare the opposite is, frankly, insulting.

Sorry for the long rant, but as a relatively new Voater, this place is great, and I wanted to be explicit about what I think makes it that way, and why Reddit now sucks.
